title: What a Granite Ridge Pass Account Still Shows to Collect and the Share Taken on the Charge Retained
content:
How much of the amount placed on a Granite Ridge Season Pass Programme pass account is still to be collected raises the share at which the figure carried into that step is taken.

**First.** Where the amount the pass account still shows to collect is at least ninety-five in the hundred — a share of 0.95 or more — of the amount placed on it when the instalment plan was opened, that figure is taken at once and a quarter, a multiple of 1.25.

**Second.** Where the amount the pass account still shows to collect is at least eighty but below ninety-five in the hundred — a share of 0.8 or more but below 0.95 — of the amount placed on it when the instalment plan was opened, that figure is taken at once and a tenth, a multiple of 1.1.

**Otherwise.** In any other case the figure is not raised by this rule.

### The share read off the pass account

The share is the amount the pass account still shows to collect set against the amount placed on it when the instalment plan was opened.

| Amount placed on the account when the plan was opened | Amount still to be collected | Share | Multiple taken |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1200.00 | 1150.00 | above 0.95 | 1.25 |
| 1200.00 | 1140.00 | exactly 0.95 | 1.25 |
| 1200.00 | 1000.00 | between 0.8 and 0.95 | 1.1 |
| 1200.00 | 960.00 | exactly 0.8 | 1.1 |
| 1200.00 | 900.00 | below 0.8 | not raised by this rule |

A pass account on which no amount was placed to be collected by instalments carries a share of nothing, and the figure is not raised by this rule.

### Worked on a hypothetical account

A pass account on which 1200.00 was placed when the plan was opened and which still shows 1150.00 to collect. The share stands above 0.95, so a figure of 200.00 carried into this step is taken at a multiple of 1.25, which gives 250.00.
